title: feat(story): add native HTML walkthroughs and 1080p video export
body:
## Problem and value

Existing native diagrams already contain a reading order, relationships, legends and source evidence, but Live/Still and the current motion recording do not explain a system as a sequence of focused scenes. Producing that walkthrough separately makes an AI rewrite presentation, camera, audio and export code for each diagram.

This adds an opt-in `archify story scan / draft / attach` workflow. An AI reads a source map and writes a compact JSON brief containing selected source IDs and explanation text. The runtime supplies framing, native animation, local relationship drawings, captions, synchronized music/action cues and video export. Existing HTML gains a Story option on its motion control, a draggable playback timeline and **Story video** in its original Export menu (1920×1080, 60 fps, VP9/Opus WebM).

- **Scope proposal:** #1045, opened following the maintainer request; scope agreement remains pending.
- This supports native Archify HTML and all ten diagram families. It does not infer a business explanation from topology: the brief's author owns that explanation.
- Before/after reproduction is below. No speech synthesis or measured token/performance improvement is claimed.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: investigation, design, implementation, tests, review and documentation.
- Tools/models: Codex (`gpt-6.1-sol`); `gpt-6-luna` with max reasoning for actual Skill-driven authoring trials using existing diagrams and a separate code-backed diagram.
- Accountable contributor: @goatliamia.
- Problem origin: proposed improvement, iterated through actual local playback and authoring trials; export lifecycle and audio timestamp defects were found during pre-PR checks.
- [x] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded below.

## Stability impact

- New CLI, browser runtime, authoring instructions and packaged assets: conservative full regression/package/browser impact.
- Attachment preserves the original native document bytes, graph and notes. Playback loads on demand. Existing themes and all four visual presets automatically propagate to Story; export freezes the selected appearance. Attached playback and its controls consume the native palette; the brief accent belongs to standalone presentation styling. A custom brief color does not override native preset/theme ownership. Existing renderers, typed inputs and native layout remain unchanged.
- Publication reuses existing path/atomic-output protections. Invalid IDs, input/output aliases and missing code evidence preserve inputs and previous output. Optional code excerpts require a repository root and verified pinned ranges.
- Focused complexity review kept one motion authority: Story's native-motion asset is generated from the existing Viewer source. The bundled HTML parser runs only in Node and includes its licenses; no runtime npm installation is required.
- Test-value review added real encode/decode coverage. It exposed and fixed a detached-frame Blob ownership bug and repeated Opus flushes that produced overlapping audio timestamps. Existing canonical exports and native document preservation are checked through the public path.

- Review follow-up (`7ef3561b`): parsed attachment boundaries, non-object brief diagnostics, owned companion rollback, source language and English controls, system reduced-motion handling for interactive playback, and Blob-part WebM muxing with a bounded export buffer. Oversized ranges fail before rendering; ordinary 110-second ranges pass preflight. Video files retain authored motion.

- Incremental follow-up (`66f8376d`): stream playback through two scheduled 4-second buffers; retain original publication diagnostics when rollback release fails; preserve the native Live/Still storage contract for user clicks; use a neutral default eyebrow. The 1080p/60 fps VP9 declaration now uses [level 4.1](https://www.webmproject.org/vp9/levels/).
- Accent follow-up (`84b468c3`): validate the optional color before CSS interpolation. Invalid declarations, URL-bearing values and non-color input fail before publication; literal hex colors remain accepted. The regression reproduced success before the fix and now verifies failure with preserved output.

- Localized-control follow-up (`056fa63d`): native Live/Still labels use the existing Viewer catalog, including custom translations. Three Story-specific strings extend that lookup for six bundled locales with English fallback; remaining English controls declare their language. Chrome and Edge cover six bundled locales plus a custom French catalog, all three modes, native appearance and actual media export. Thirteen Story Node tests, three doctor cases and extracted-package smoke also passed.

- URL/audio follow-up (`7daa2504`): encode the editable-brief file URL instead of treating path characters as URL syntax, with an explicit relative prefix or cross-volume file URL. Export PCM synthesis and its budget now cover only the requested interval. Fourteen Story Node tests, Chrome/Edge playback and a real late video clip with FFmpeg decode, extracted-package smoke and ZIP/index checks passed. The POSIX-only scheme-like filename regression is included for Linux CI.

- Lifecycle follow-up (`001c658c`): register each committed draft output before releasing its handle, roll back the owned pair on failure, and continue temporary-file cleanup while preserving the original error. Diagnostics distinguish a rejected publication from a completed publication with cleanup failure. Story camera policy now reads the native motion governor. The `52c9377a` compatibility follow-up applies the isolated render policy to browser CSSOM media rules, including styles from earlier native HTML, and excludes background-document suspension during frame seeking. No stylesheet selector exceptions or input rewrites are needed. Ordinary interactive preferences and ownership protections remain intact.

- Maintainer follow-up (`c14173a7`): post-commit publication warnings now fail the command while retaining committed ownership, cleanup details and recovery paths in both plain-text and JSON errors. Generated opening/closing chapter labels use neutral numbering; authored labels remain intact. In the shipped attachment load path, only the isolated export srcdoc receives `data-motion-render`. Chrome and Edge now verify that an unenhanced native page, the enhanced native view and interactive Story playback retain their reduced-motion rules and suppress native transfers, while the isolated render frame retains camera/transfer motion. Export completion leaves both interactive stylesheets and policies unchanged. No shared Viewer runtime change was needed in this follow-up.

- Audio-envelope follow-up (`3ffeed8a`): partial exports now pass the full Story duration to the shared audio renderer while synthesizing only the requested interval. The regression failed on `c14173a7` and passes after the one-argument fix. It compares both channels at the real AudioEncoder boundary against the same preview interval, while retaining allocation bounds and real WebM/FFmpeg decode coverage. Chrome and Edge passed the affected public Story integration. The flowless-edge finding was investigated separately and is not changed by this commit.

## Tests run

Base: `e49cfd2a` (`dev`); current candidate: `3ffeed8a83f2ec67432d7bb2d8692f637f2f9c30`.

| Evidence | Revision / result |
| --- | --- |
| Partial-export audio regression | Chrome and Edge public Story integration passed on `3ffeed8a`: all 9,600 stereo PCM samples in a short late export agree with the preview interval within 1e-6, with bounded synthesis and real WebM/FFmpeg decode. The new assertion failed on parent `c14173a7` |
| Focused Story Node checks | 21 passed on `c14173a7`, including committed previous-handle release and retained-backup cleanup failures, recovery-path reporting and owned rollback. Existing concurrent-writer preservation checks remain in place |
| Real Chrome and Edge Story integration | Both complete Story browser suites passed on `c14173a7`: seven locale cases, neutral chapter numbering, authored labels, isolated export motion, unchanged interactive reduced-motion CSS/policies, native appearance, bounded playback, PNG and real 1080p/60 fps video with FFmpeg audio decode |
| FFmpeg decode of the actual Story export | Passed: stereo audio, requested interval and timestamps |
| Release/package gates | Previous-head CI at `52c9377a` passed the broad package/platform and published-manifest gates. Current candidate passed the canonical local ZIP/index check and extracted-package smoke; its remote CI is tracked below. No release or installation was performed |
| Package smoke without dependencies | Current candidate passed on Windows from a freshly extracted ZIP, including the public Story scan/draft/attach chain. Previous-head CI passed on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows |
| Canonical Node 22 ZIP and public-content checks | 221 files; all 220 untransformed package entries match staged Git bytes; whitespace and sensitive-content checks passed |
| Affected shared checks | 408 passed, 4 POSIX-only checks skipped on Windows: core product, atomic-output protection, Viewer generation and Architecture comparison. Native governor browser checks cover all ten families. The inherited-style fix reran Chrome/Edge integration, 326 Viewer/README checks and generated-output/golden freshness; all passed. The 12-artifact Gallery and README proof were rebuilt |
| Remote integration | [Current-head CI](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/39556279465) is queued/running at `3ffeed8a83f2ec67432d7bb2d8692f637f2f9c30`. [Parent-head CI](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/39553193997) passed all 19 executed jobs at `c14173a7`; reuse applies only to unchanged behavior |

The first lifecycle follow-up [run](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/39546675544) failed because the README motion-proof source digests were stale after the Gallery rebuild. Commit `2bd526ef` genuinely rebuilds the GIF and its receipt; all 15 README showcase checks passed locally. No runtime or test relaxation was used to address that failure.

The first CI attempt on `7ef3561b` exposed an existing parallel-fixture race: catalog enrollment copied the live package while the archive-negative test removed its temporary link (`ENOENT`). Only failed jobs were rerun, successfully; the original failure remains in run history. Those unrelated tests were not changed.

The initial Windows full-suite run at `3c0bfee8` was not green (3,115 passed, 30 failed, 53 cancelled, 155 skipped). Seven package/toolchain failures passed after the environment was corrected. The other 23 failures and 53 cancellations reproduced on unchanged `dev` (Windows path/8.3 assertions, Git null-device configuration and notifier fixtures). The complete remote CI at `66f8376d` supplies the later broad integration evidence; it is not represented as a local full-suite pass. Current changes reuse unaffected generation evidence and rerun their focused browser, audio and publication boundaries.

Native diagram generation is unchanged. The actual Skill-driven authoring trials are workflow usability evidence, not a paired generation benchmark or maintainer scope approval.

## Visual evidence

Reproduce from the public packaged workflow:

```sh
node archify/bin/archify.mjs story draft archify/examples/workflow-agent-tool-call-rendered.html brief.json --json
```

Replace `brief.json` with:

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "title": "Permission before execution",
  "intro": "Locate the planner, router and approval gate in the complete workflow.",
  "outro": "The approval gate separates choosing a capability from executing it.",
  "scenes": [{
    "title": "A selected tool may require permission",
    "points": [{
      "anchor": "approval",
      "via": "approval-check",
      "title": "The gate controls whether execution proceeds",
      "text": "The router has selected a capability. This boundary lets a policy or human decision hold execution, with denial leading to the recovery branch.",
      "caption": "Follow the router's handoff to the approval gate."
    }]
  }]
}
```

```sh
node archify/bin/archify.mjs story attach archify/examples/workflow-agent-tool-call-rendered.html brief.json workflow-story.html --json
```

Open the result, cycle the native motion button to Story, scrub its timeline, change theme/preset, return to the native diagram and inspect Export → Story video. The original cards remain available below playback. Compare with the unchanged input in the same browser, viewport and appearance.

Automated checks cover all four presets × both themes, preserved source content/controls, seeking, rapid mode switches, a frozen-appearance 1080p PNG and an actual 1080p/60 fps video with audio. Chrome and Edge were exercised. Local visual iterations were inspected during development; this is not a claim of maintainer perceptual acceptance. Other browser engines were not tested; video export requires supported WebCodecs encoders.

## Generated artifacts

- Added `archify/story/native-motion.js`, generated from `viewer/motion-governor.js` and covered by freshness checks.
- Rebuilt `archify.zip` with canonical Node 22/zlib; 221 package files, no experimental runs or local-only artifacts.
- Regenerated the Viewer template, native diagram goldens, Gallery and Checkout comparison from tracked sources; genuinely rebuilt the README motion GIF and its source receipt. Release version is unchanged; this PR performs no release or installation.
